label: Film and Screen
blurb: Movies, taken seriously enough to have a shelf, a list and an opinion about which cut is the right one.

nodes.label: Horror
nodes.blurb: The genre with the deepest subgenre map and the most committed people arguing about it. You can like several of them and dislike the rest.

nodes.label: Physical Media
nodes.blurb: Boutique labels, restorations and the transfer that finally looks the way it did in a cinema. Owning it because streaming keeps removing it.

nodes.label: Science Fiction
nodes.blurb: From the model-and-motion-control era to whatever is rendered now. The genre most likely to send a viewer to a workbench.

nodes.label: Kaiju and Tokusatsu
nodes.blurb: Suit actors, miniature cities and pyrotechnics. Practical effects taken to their most committed conclusion.

nodes.label: Animation
nodes.blurb: Cel, stop motion and everything after. A medium the rest of the shelf keeps mistaking for a genre.

nodes.label: Noir and Crime
nodes.blurb: Low key lighting, worse people, and a run of films short enough that you can actually see most of it.

nodes.label: Documentary
nodes.blurb: The genre that most often turns a viewer into a participant, because somebody on screen is doing something you could do.

nodes.label: Film History
nodes.blurb: Watching by director, movement or decade instead of by whatever is on. The point where a habit becomes a subject.

nodes.label: Logging and Lists
nodes.blurb: Recording what you watched and what you thought. A hobby's memory, and the reason you can tell what a year actually looked like.

nodes.label: Writing About Film
nodes.blurb: Four hundred words that make somebody watch a film they had dismissed. Harder than it looks, and cheap to try.

nodes.label: Festivals
nodes.blurb: Watching four in a day with people who chose the same four. Where the recommendations for the next year come from.

nodes.label: Soundtracks
nodes.blurb: Scores on vinyl and the composers people follow across films. A second collection that grows out of the first.

nodes.label: Home Cinema
nodes.blurb: Projector, screen, speakers and a room you can make properly dark. The gear rabbit hole attached to the watching.

nodes.label: Film Projection
nodes.blurb: Running actual 16mm or 35mm at home. A mechanical repair hobby wearing a film hobby's coat.

nodes.label: Practical Effects
nodes.blurb: Miniatures, animatronics, latex and squibs. Studying how the shot was faked is one short step from building props yourself.

edges.note: Nobody asks how a shot was done more often than a horror viewer looking at a creature.
